541: A, C, and E are correct. A is correct because API Gateway with a Lambda function and DynamoDB is a fully serverless backend that scales from zero and costs almost nothing while request volume is unpredictable and idle, which is far more cost-effective than always-running containers. C is correct because a Cognito user pool provides managed sign-up, sign-in, and authentication, which enforces that only customers who paid a subscription fee can sign in and use the application. E is correct because AWS Amplify serves the static HTML, CSS, and JS frontend with integrated CloudFront distribution, providing low-cost managed static hosting with global content delivery. Together these choices avoid paying for idle compute and unmanaged servers that PHP hosting or a fleet of containers would require.
542: B is correct because CloudFront signed URLs provide time-limited access to specific content delivered through the distribution, which matches granting premium customers on-demand access to individual items such as a movie rental or a music download. Each signed URL targets a single file, so access can be controlled and expired per customer per item while the S3 origin remains locked down. Signed cookies would be the choice for serving many files at once rather than specific on-demand items, and origin access control only blocks direct S3 access without authenticating customers.
543: A and D are correct. A is correct because Savings Plan discount sharing is turned on in the billing preferences of the management account in AWS Organizations, which allows the Savings Plan rates to apply to eligible usage across all member accounts in the organization. D is correct because Savings Plan discounts can only be shared among accounts in the same organization, so creating an organization in a new dedicated payer account and inviting the individually billed accounts consolidates them under one management account. Using a new payer account keeps the management account free of existing workloads and billing history, which is the recommended best practice for the organization management account.
544: A is correct because API Gateway canary release deployment sends a small, configurable percentage of production traffic to the new version while the remaining traffic stays on the stable stage, so any defect affects only that fraction of customers. After the new version is verified, the canary is promoted so the full traffic gradually shifts to the new version. Because the traffic shift happens within the same stage and custom domain name behind the same Route 53 alias record, customers see no endpoint change and data loss is minimized.
545: B is correct because a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration uses health checks to keep all traffic on the ALB while it is healthy and automatically routes traffic to a static error page hosted in an S3 bucket when the ALB endpoint is unhealthy. This solution requires only DNS configuration and an S3 static site, with no extra EC2 instances or infrastructure to maintain, so it minimizes both changes and operational overhead.
546: D is correct because the Storage Gateway tape gateway exposes an iSCSI virtual tape library interface, so the existing on-premises backup applications and workflows continue to operate unchanged while the virtual tapes are stored in Amazon S3 and Amazon Glacier instead of on physical tape. This preserves the existing investment in backup software, eliminates physical tapes, and lowers costs by moving long-term backup storage to the cloud.
547: A is correct because Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, serverless delivery stream that scales automatically to capture high-volume sensor data in near real time and load it continuously into Amazon S3. It requires no infrastructure to provision and no custom code for scaling or batching, which gives the least operational overhead. The other options would require building and operating custom pipelines to handle continuous streaming ingestion.
548: B is correct because service control policies in AWS Organizations are the native, centrally managed mechanism to restrict which AWS service actions are available in member accounts, and they apply regardless of IAM permissions inside those accounts. Creating an organizational unit for each department and attaching SCPs to those OUs enforces the restrictions from the management account with no agents or per-account tooling, which provides the least operational overhead.
549: B is correct because a managed NAT gateway in the public subnets lets the MySQL cluster in the private subnets initiate outbound connections to the third-party internet provider while blocking all unsolicited inbound connections, maximizing security for the database tier. Updating the private subnet route table to send internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway implements this with a fully managed AWS service, so it adds security without the operational overhead of patching and managing a NAT instance. Routing the private subnets directly to an internet gateway would expose the database to the internet.
550: B and D are correct. B is correct because the Lambda execution role is the identity the function assumes, so it must be granted KMS decrypt permission to read the encrypted environment variables at invocation. D is correct because access to a KMS key is governed by its resource-based key policy, so the key policy must explicitly allow the Lambda execution role to perform decryption; both the identity-based permission on the role and the resource-based allowance on the key are required for the decryption to succeed.
551: A is correct because S3 Standard handles the frequent access during the first week, and a lifecycle rule that transitions the reports to S3 Glacier after 7 days provides very low-cost storage for the several-year retention period. S3 Glacier standard retrievals complete within 3 to 5 hours, which satisfies the 6-hour retrievability requirement, whereas Glacier Deep Archive retrievals can take up to 12 hours and would violate that requirement. This combination is therefore the most cost-effective option that still meets the retrieval window.
552: B is correct because a Compute Savings Plan automatically applies its discount to any EC2 instance family, size, OS, or Region, and even to Fargate and Lambda usage, giving maximum flexibility while still reducing cost. This flexibility lets the company change instance types and families every 2 to 3 months without losing the discount. Reserved Instances and EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to specific instance attributes or families, so they cannot accommodate frequent changes in instance type and family.
553: A is correct because Amazon Macie is a fully managed service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and classify sensitive data such as personally identifiable information stored in Amazon S3 buckets. Macie is a regional service, so enabling it in us-east-1 and us-west-2 and creating a sensitive data discovery job in each Region analyzes the stored data with no infrastructure to run or maintain. The other services do not scan S3 object content for PII.
554: C is correct because memory optimized instance families, such as the R family, are designed with high memory-to-vCPU ratios for memory-intensive workloads. The on-premises performance data shows both the SAP application and the SQL Server database have high memory utilization, so running both tiers on memory optimized instances directly matches the workload profile and meets the high demands of the SAP database.
555: A is correct because an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS places an elastic network interface in the selected subnets, letting the EC2 instances in the private subnets reach the queue entirely over private IP addresses without traversing the internet. Configuring the endpoint in the private subnets and attaching a security group with an inbound rule allowing traffic from those EC2 instances ensures only the application instances can connect to the queue. Note that SQS only supports interface endpoints, since gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.
556: B is correct because an IAM role with the required DynamoDB read and write permissions, delivered to the application instances through an EC2 instance profile, lets the application automatically obtain short-lived temporary credentials from the instance metadata. This approach avoids embedding or passing any access keys or secrets through the CloudFormation template or user data, meeting the security requirement with no credential exposure.
557: B is correct because Amazon EMR provides managed big data frameworks such as Spark that process large semistructured S3 datasets in parallel across a resizable cluster, satisfying the parallel processing requirement. The same EMR cluster can join and enrich the processed data with information stored in Amazon Redshift, so both the processing and enrichment requirements are met with a single service.
558: C is correct because a VPC peering connection is a point-to-point network link between two VPCs with no hourly attachment fees and no per-GB data processing charges, making it the cheapest way to connect exactly two VPCs in the same Region and account. A transit gateway charges per attachment hour and per GB processed and is cost justified only when many VPCs or transitive routing are needed. VPN tunnels and Direct Connect add unnecessary cost and complexity for same-Region inter-VPC traffic.
559: B and E are correct. B is correct because the tags the teams applied to their compute resources are user-defined cost allocation tags, which must be selected in the AWS Billing console so that cost reports can group consolidated billing data by product line. E is correct because cost allocation tags in an organization must be activated from the Organizations management account, which applies the tag activation across all member accounts so their tagged usage appears in the consolidated billing reports. Activating tags individually in each member account is not how consolidated billing cost tracking works.
560: A is correct because AWS Control Tower governs accounts and organizational units in AWS Organizations and continuously monitors the registered landing zone configuration, automatically detecting drift such as changes to the OU hierarchy. Control Tower sends built-in drift notifications to the operations team through its integrated governance workflow, so no custom rules, pipelines, or manual analysis are needed, which provides the least operational overhead.
